title: Compiler Hunt: Strict Go
story: This Go file will not compile. Be the compiler and spot every line it rejects.
goal: Tap every line the compiler would reject.

tests.label: Find every bad line, then pick the fix

hints: Read for unused variables, missing imports and type mismatches.
socratic: Which line uses something that was never declared or imported?
Which line is declared but never used?
Compare your result with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what does the Go compiler enforce here?

why_lines.5: The "os" package is imported but never used. Go refuses to compile that.
why_lines.9: `unused` is declared and never used. Go treats that as an error.

fix.question: How do you fix this file?
options: Add a semicolon after each line
Remove the unused import and the unused variable
fix.why: Go keeps code tidy: remove what you do not use.
